newsitem.title: UK: Cuba, Thailand prevail as sugar freight origins.
newsitem.headline: Cuba, Thailand prevail as sugar freight origins.

text.p: Cuba and Thailand were most in demand as origins on the sugar freight market on Thursday but new orders were relatively scarce as fixtures dominated business, shipbrokers said.
The only new inquiry to emerge was for Cuban bulk raw sugar, with Pacol and Jean Lion both quoting for 30,000 tonnes apiece to Iran for early February.
Shipbrokers said Mauritius Sugar Syndicate fixed the 1977-built Kavo Alexandros, 26,414 dwt and carrying a Greek flag, to ship 18,500 tonnes min/max bulk sugar on its usual Port Louis-London run.
The rate was stg 15.00, not stg 16.00 as recently reported, they said.
Cargill was said to be closely working its bagged order for 12/14,000 tonnes from Thailand to South Korea or Indonesia for the first half of February.
It was also working a previous bulk order for 8,000 tonnes from Thailand to Japan for early March.
Shipbrokers noted Indonesian demand for Thai bagged sugar and pointed to two fixtures -- Louis Dreyfus with 14,300 tonnes and Glencore with 12,000.
Details of the rates achieved for either fixture have yet to emerge.
Express Sea Transport was believed to be firm with some timecharter business from Caribs to Med, with the size thought to be in the region of 20,000 tonnes, market sources said.
